visual_review.finding: The milder aligned lens visibly enlarges the same central printed target and preserves recognizable bars; the scene and wrist-camera framing agree with the earlier realtime proof.

findings: Aligned100 passes the unchanged metric in both renderers. PathTracing gains are 1.90466x native and 1.90692x policy; differences from RealTimePathTracing are 0.3193% and 0.0640%, respectively.
The same pattern transitions are observed: native 1.2 mm bars and policy 2.4 mm bars become resolved in both orientations under the conservative development criterion.
The IOR=1 control remains at approximately 1.00x in both image sizes; tilt loses the target; the strongly curved lens remains unsuitable for uniform-gain interpretation.

All five completed cases match their saved array hashes and PNGs. The runner records actual policy-wrapper equality and unchanged joints. The missing baseline repeat is disclosed; no complete-run claim is made.
This independent rendering reference corroborates static native refraction and useful policy-input detail. It does not validate physical optical calibration or a manipulation task.
